blocks.text: OrbitAvanya Tech LLP is pleased to submit this proposal in response to Solicitation N0016426SNB94 for IT Services. As a technology services firm specializing in enterprise software development, cloud-native architectures, AI/ML systems, and e-Governance digital transformation, we are uniquely positioned to deliver the comprehensive IT services required by the Issuing Agency. Our team brings deep expertise across the full software development lifecycle — from requirements engineering and architecture design through development, testing, deployment, and ongoing operations — using modern technology stacks including React, Next.js, Python/FastAPI, Node.js, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and AWS. We understand that federal IT services demand rigorous adherence to security standards, compliance frameworks, and software quality practices. Our approach integrates **NIST 800-53** security controls, **FedRAMP**-aligned cloud practices, **CMMI**-inspired process discipline, and **Agile/DevSecOps** methodologies to ensure rapid, secure, and sustainable delivery. This proposal outlines our technical approach, proposed solution architecture, delivery methodology, team capabilities, and pricing structure designed to meet the Agency's mission objectives while reducing technical debt, improving system resilience, and accelerating digital modernization.

blocks.text: The Issuing Agency's requirement for IT Services under NAICS 541511 reflects the ongoing federal imperative to modernize legacy systems, strengthen cybersecurity posture, and deliver citizen-centric digital services. As agencies navigate the **OMB M-23-22** modernization directives, **Executive Order 14028** on cybersecurity, and the **Federal Data Strategy**, the need for a partner that combines technical depth with federal acquisition and compliance fluency is paramount. OrbitAvanya Tech LLP recognizes that this engagement is not merely about staff augmentation — it is about delivering measurable mission outcomes through technology. Our strategic approach aligns with the **Technology Modernization Fund (TMF)** principles: user-centered design, modular contracting, incremental delivery, and outcome-based metrics. We position ourselves as a mission partner capable of spanning the full spectrum from legacy system sustainment to greenfield cloud-native development, ensuring continuity of operations while progressively reducing technical debt and operational risk.
Finding 1 · Legacy System Modernization Imperative

Federal agencies typically operate heterogeneous portfolios containing mainframe, client-server, and early-web-era applications that inhibit agility, increase security surface area, and consume disproportionate O&M budgets. Modernization must proceed incrementally to avoid mission disruption.

items: Identify **high-value, low-risk** candidates for **strangler fig** migration patterns
Prioritize **API-first** decomposition to enable frontend modernization independent of backend
Leverage **containerization** for lift-and-shift where refactoring ROI is low
Establish **automated regression suites** before any code modification

blocks.text: Finding 2 · Cloud Adoption and Security Compliance

Cloud migration in the federal space requires strict adherence to **FedRAMP** authorization boundaries, **NIST 800-53** control inheritance, and **CISA** binding operational directives. A shared responsibility model must be clearly defined and continuously monitored.

items: Design **landing zone** architecture with **AWS Control Tower** or equivalent
Align with **Zero Trust Architecture** per **OMB M-22-09**

blocks.text: Finding 3 · Data Interoperability and Analytics

Siloed data across program offices limits evidence-based decision making. Modern data platforms must support **FAIR principles** (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) while enforcing **privacy** and **PII/PHI** protections.

items: Deploy **data mesh** or **lakehouse** architecture on **AWS Lake Formation** / **Redshift**
Integrate **MLOps** pipelines for **predictive modeling** and **anomaly detection**

blocks.text: Finding 4 · DevSecOps Maturity and Software Supply Chain Security
Software supply chain attacks (e.g., **SolarWinds**, **Log4j**) mandate **SBOM** generation, **artifact signing**, **dependency scanning**, and **policy-as-code** enforcement across the pipeline.

items: Integrate **Syft/Grype**, **Trivy**, **Snyk** into **CI/CD** (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CodePipeline)
Enforce **SLSA Level 3** build provenance and **Sigstore** signing
Maintain **real-time vulnerability dashboards** with **CISA KEV** correlation

blocks.text: Finding 5 · Accessibility and User-Centered Design

Federal digital services must comply with **Section 508** and **WCAG 2.1 AA**. Accessibility cannot be an afterthought; it must be embedded in design systems, component libraries, and acceptance criteria.

items: Integrate **axe-core** and **Lighthouse CI** in PR gates
Conduct **moderated usability testing** with **assistive technology users**

blocks.text: Finding 6 · Workforce Enablement and Knowledge Transfer

Sustainable outcomes require that Agency staff can operate, extend, and govern delivered solutions. Contractor dependency must be systematically reduced through documentation, training, and co-development models.

items: Establish **inner source** practices with **shared repositories** and **RFC processes**
Execute **pair programming** and **mob reviews** with Government technical leads

blocks.text: The scope of this engagement encompasses the full spectrum of IT services required to modernize, secure, and sustain the Agency's application and infrastructure portfolio. Services are organized into five core workstreams: (1) **Application Development & Modernization** — design, development, testing, and deployment of web, mobile, and API services using modern frameworks; (2) **Cloud Platform Engineering** — landing zone operations, infrastructure as code, environment management, and cost optimization on AWS; (3) **DevSecOps & Release Management** — pipeline engineering, security automation, release orchestration, and software supply chain hardening; (4) **Data & Analytics Platform** — data integration, warehousing, visualization, and ML enablement; and (5) **Cybersecurity & Compliance Operations** — continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, audit support, and Zero Trust implementation. Each workstream operates under a unified **SAFe 6.0** governance model with **PI cadence**, **epic/feature/backlog hierarchy**, and **outcome-based OKRs**. The engagement supports both **greenfield development** and **brownfield sustainment**, with transition planning for legacy system divestiture. All work adheres to **FAR/DFARS** clauses, **NIST 800-53 Rev. 5** control implementation, **FedRAMP** continuous monitoring, and **Agency-specific** policies.

blocks.text: OrbitAvanya Tech LLP proposes a **modular, platform-centric solution** built on three foundational pillars: **Developer Experience (DevEx) Platform**, **Compliance Automation Fabric**, and **Data & Intelligence Layer**. The DevEx Platform provides a **golden path** for application teams — standardized **Terraform modules**, **Helm charts**, **CI/CD templates**, **observability stacks** (Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo), and **self-service provisioning** via **Backstage** or **ServiceNow** integration. This reduces cognitive load, enforces guardrails by default, and accelerates **time-to-first-commit** from weeks to hours. The Compliance Automation Fabric embeds **NIST 800-53** controls into the infrastructure and pipeline layers: **Config Rules** map to **AC, AU, CM, SC, SI** families; **Security Hub** findings auto-generate **POA&M entries** with **Jira** integration; **Lambda-based** evidence collectors package **FedRAMP** artifacts continuously. This shifts compliance **left** and **down**, eliminating point-in-time audit scrambles. The Data & Intelligence Layer implements a **domain-oriented data mesh** on **AWS**: **producer-owned** data products published to a **central catalog** (Glue/Amundsen), **consumer self-service** via **Athena/Redshift/QuickSight**, **federated governance** with **Lake Formation** permissions, and **MLOps** pipelines for **forecasting, classification, anomaly detection**. Applications are architected as **modular monoliths** or **microservices** based on **bounded context** analysis, communicating via **async event-driven** patterns (EventBridge/Kafka) and **sync REST/gRPC** with **API Gateway** management. **Frontends** leverage **Next.js App Router** with **React Server Components** for performance, **USWDS** for compliance, and **Storybook** for component governance. **Security** is pervasive: **WAF** with **managed rules**, **Shield Advanced** for DDoS, **Secrets Manager** with **automatic rotation**, **Certificate Manager** for **mTLS**, **IAM** with **least-privilege** and **condition keys**. **Operations** follow **SRE principles**: **SLOs/SLIs** defined per service, **error budgets** drive release velocity, **chaos engineering** (AWS FIS) validates resilience. **Knowledge transfer** is continuous — not a phase — via **inner source**, **pairing**, **ADRs**, and **quarterly architecture reviews** with Government stakeholders.

blocks.text: Technology Stack

The proposed engagement follows a **phased, incremental approach** aligned with **SAFe Program Increments (PIs)** of 8–10 weeks each. Phase 0 (Mobilization) establishes governance, tooling, and baseline assessments in the first 2 weeks. Subsequent PIs deliver **minimum viable capabilities (MVCs)** every 8–10 weeks, with **System Demos** at the end of each PI for stakeholder validation. This cadence ensures early value delivery, continuous feedback, and risk reduction. The timeline below represents the first **three PIs (24–30 weeks)**; subsequent PIs are planned during **PI Planning** events with Government Product Owners.

blocks.text: Total Estimated Duration: 24–30 Weeks for Initial Delivery (3 PIs); Ongoing Multi-Year Engagement

OrbitAvanya Tech LLP proposes a **hybrid pricing model** combining **Fixed-Price** for well-defined deliverables (platform setup, migrations, compliance artifacts) and **Time & Materials (T&M)** for capacity-based services (development capacity, Tier 3 support, emerging requirements). This aligns with **OMB M-18-18** guidance on modular contracting and **FAR 16.505** ordering procedures. Pricing reflects **fully burdened labor rates** by labor category (LCAT), **AWS consumption** passed through at cost with **FinOps governance**, and **travel/ODC** per **FAR 31.2**. Rates are based on **GSA MAS / GWAC** benchmarks and are **negotiable** based on volume, term, and risk sharing. A **Not-to-Exceed (NTE)** ceiling is established per PI with **earned value management (EVM)** reporting for transparency.
Service Level Agreement & Terms

items: **Incident Response**: P1 (Critical) < 1 hour acknowledgment, < 4 hour resolution; P2 (High) < 2 hour acknowledgment, < 8 hour resolution; P3 (Medium) < 4 hour acknowledgment, < 24 hour resolution; P4 (Low) < 1 business day acknowledgment, < 5 business days resolution
**Change Success Rate**: ≥ 95% of standard changes successful; ≥ 90% of emergency changes successful
**Deployment Frequency**: On-demand for standard changes via automated pipeline; emergency changes < 2 hours
**Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)**: < 2 hours for P1, < 8 hours for P2
**Security Patch Deployment**: Critical (CVSS ≥ 9.0) within 72 hours; High (CVSS 7.0–8.9) within 14 days; Medium/Low within 30 days
**Vulnerability Scan Remediation**: Critical findings < 30 days; High < 60 days; Medium < 90 days
**Backup & Recovery**: RPO ≤ 1 hour (RDS, DynamoDB PITR), RTO ≤ 4 hours (validated quarterly)
**Capacity Headroom**: Minimum 30% headroom on compute, storage, database; auto-scaling configured for all production workloads
**Compliance Reporting**: Monthly **POA&M** updates; Quarterly **Security Hub** posture report; Annual **FISMA/FedRAMP** package
